chapter_name: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
learning_objective: 🏺 Discover the fascinating urban planning, mysterious script, and eventual decline of the ancient Harappan Civilisation!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Harappan cities were divided into a smaller, higher Citadel (for public buildings) and a larger Lower Town. They featured a brilliant grid system for streets and an incredibly advanced drainage system built with baked bricks.

Harappans ate a wide range of plant and animal products. They grew wheat, barley, lentils, chickpeas, and sesame. Animal bones of cattle, sheep, goat, and pig indicate they domesticated these animals.

Harappan seals contain a script that remains undeciphered to this day. It was written from right to left and contained between 375 to 400 signs, making it a logo-syllabic script rather than alphabetical.

Exchanges were regulated by a precise system of weights, usually made of a stone called chert and generally cubical, with no markings. The lower denominations were binary, while higher ones followed the decimal system.

Around 1800 BCE, most mature Harappan sites were abandoned. The reasons are debated but likely include climate change, deforestation, excessive floods, the shifting/drying up of rivers, or overuse of the landscape.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Be an Archaeologist
fun_activity.instructions: Look closely at the 'Priest King' statue or the 'Dancing Girl' bronze figure from Mohenjodaro online. Notice the intricate details like the trefoil pattern on the priest's shawl and the bangles on the dancing girl's arm—these tell us volumes about their textile and metallurgical skills!

exam_tips: 📌 Always highlight the drainage system and grid-pattern streets when asked about Harappan urban planning.
📌 Remember that the Harappan script is still undeciphered; any mention of what their texts say is just historical speculation based on symbols.
📌 Distinguish between the 'Citadel' (smaller, higher, public structures like the Great Bath) and the 'Lower Town' (larger, residential).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Harappan Civilisation is also known as the Indus Valley Civilisation, named after the first discovered site, Harappa.
⭐ Steatite was the most common stone used to make Harappan seals.
⭐ The 'Great Bath' was a large rectangular tank in a courtyard, likely used for special ritual baths.
